output.summary: Proposed visual direction for Imvusa Furniture: a warm, tactile, upscale-but-approachable design system supporting a two-location South African custom furniture, reupholstery and interior services brand. Built to showcase craftsmanship (leather, fabric, wood) through editorial photography and generous whitespace, with a single canonical contact/quote funnel per the site blueprint.
output.direction:
DISCLOSURE: This is a genuinely blind run. I have no browsing capability and no image-analysis tool in this environment, and I have not seen and cannot see the actual Imvusa site, its leather couch photography, gallery images, or any real brand assets (logo, existing color usage, fonts). Everything below is a proposed starting hypothesis derived only from the text of the research_report and site_blueprint (positioning: custom furniture / reupholstery / interior services, craftsmanship-led, warm and upscale-but-approachable, two South African regional locations, Hertex Fabrics partnership). Every palette, typography, spacing, component and imagery recommendation in this artifact MUST be verified by a human against real site photography, the actual leather couch and gallery imagery, and any existing brand guidelines before it is treated as approved. Do not implement any of this in code or design tooling without that human visual verification step, per the BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL pipeline.

Design rationale (hypothesis): the brand sits between artisanal craftsmanship and everyday accessibility - it should feel like a well-made leather couch in a warm living room, not a cold corporate showroom. The system leans on warm neutrals and leather/wood-inspired tones, a confident-but-friendly serif or slab display face paired with a clean humanist sans for body copy, generous breathing room to let photography (couches, fabric swatches, finished rooms) carry the emotional weight, and calm, trustworthy CTA color for the single 'Get a Quote' conversion path that the blueprint centers the whole site around.

palette.usage: Primary page background - warm off-white/cream to evoke natural fabric and linen, avoid stark clinical white
Card and section surfaces, subtly warmer than base background

palette.value: #6B3F2A (PROPOSED - verify against real leather/wood tones in photography)
palette.usage: Primary brand color - deep saddle-leather brown for headers, nav accents, icons
Secondary leather/tan tone for hover states and secondary accents
Warm brass/ochre accent for highlights, dividers, small decorative details
Primary call-to-action button color (e.g. Get a Quote) - warm terracotta-brick, distinct from brown palette so CTAs stand out without feeling corporate-blue
Primary body and heading text - near-black warm charcoal, not pure black
Secondary text, captions, metadata (e.g. gallery project captions, location tags)
Hairline borders, card outlines, form field borders
Form success/confirmation states (e.g. quote form submitted)
Form validation errors on Get a Quote and Contact forms

typography.family: Serif or slab-serif display face, e.g. 'Fraunces' or 'Tiempos' (PROPOSED - verify against real brand marks/logo if any exist)
typography.usage: Page titles, hero headlines, section headers - conveys craftsmanship and warmth

typography.family: Humanist sans-serif, e.g. 'Inter' or 'Source Sans 3' (PROPOSED - verify)
typography.usage: Body copy, service descriptions, form labels, navigation - optimized for legibility and approachability

typography.family: Same as font.display, slightly smaller weight (PROPOSED)
typography.usage: Pull quotes, fabric collection names (ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE), captions needing warmth

components: Primary Nav (Home, Leather Couches, Gallery, Services, Fabrics & Collections, About, Contact) with sticky Get a Quote CTA button
Hero section with full-bleed photography placeholder + headline + single primary CTA
Service Card (icon/image, title, 1-2 sentence description, 'Request a Quote' link) - single canonical instance, no duplication, per blueprint fix
Canonical Contact Block component (phone, email, address per location) reused identically across Home, Contact, and location pages to eliminate data-source mismatches
Gallery Grid with category filter chips (Reupholstery, Curtains, Headboards, Cushions, Wallpaper, Ottomans) and project caption overlay (brief, material, location)
Fabric Collection Card (collection name, representative swatch image placeholder, short description) standardized to 'Hertex Fabrics' spelling
Get a Quote multi-step form (service type, location, project description, photo upload, preferred contact method) with progress indicator
Editorial content block for Leather Couches page (material/leather-grade explainer, process steps, care guidance, featured transformation) alternating text/image layout
Footer with canonical contact block, service links, social links, and legal/privacy line
Accessible CAPTCHA/challenge component (replacing plain-text CAPTCHA prompts found in audit) with proper ARIA labeling
imageryDirection: DISCLOSURE: no real Imvusa photography has been viewed or analyzed in this run; the following is a proposed art-direction brief for human designers to apply once real site photography (leather couches, gallery projects, fabric swatches) is reviewed.
Favor warm, natural, low-contrast lighting reminiscent of a lived-in but upscale home interior - avoid harsh studio white-backgrounds.
Prioritize close-up, tactile detail shots (leather grain, stitching, fabric texture, wood joinery) alongside wider room-context shots, to reinforce craftsmanship positioning.
Leather Couches page imagery should be paired with real editorial captions (material, leather grade, process step) rather than presented as an unlabeled image wall, per blueprint direction.
Gallery imagery should be consistently captioned with project brief, material/fabric used (standardized 'Hertex Fabrics' naming), and location (George or Bloemfontein).
Fabric collection imagery (ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE) should show swatches in situ (draped on furniture) rather than flat swatch-only shots, once real assets are available for review.
Avoid stock-photo furniture imagery wherever possible; flag to human reviewers any pages currently relying on generic stock rather than real Imvusa project photography.
All final imagery choices require human visual verification against actual site/gallery photography before implementation - this agent has not seen that photography.
